variants: Tweed Heads is the northernmost town in New South Wales, at the mouth of the Tweed River, and it runs straight into Coolangatta in Queensland, so roads and buildings span the border. Point Danger Light marks the border headland, and the coast south of it runs past Fingal Head, Kingscliff and Cabarita Beach. Inland, Murwillumbah sits in the valley around Wollumbin (Mount Warning), the remnant central vent of an ancient volcano that rises to 1,157 m. The Gold Coast is 34 km away, Byron Bay 66 km and Brisbane 103 km.

At the mouth of the Tweed River, Tweed Heads is the northernmost town in New South Wales and the twin of Coolangatta across the state line. Cedar cutters settled the river in 1844, and the district later turned to dairying, sugar cane, bananas and fishing. Today the draws are the border headlands, the Tweed coast beaches and, 23 km inland by road, Murwillumbah and the caldera that surrounds Wollumbin. The 1994 film Muriel's Wedding used Tweed Heads as the fictional town of Porpoise Spit.

Tweed Heads and Coolangatta are twin towns on the New South Wales and Queensland border, and it is often not obvious which state you are standing in. The NSW side lies in Tweed Shire, whose seat Murwillumbah is a short drive inland in the valley of an ancient volcano, where the 1,157 m peak of Wollumbin (Mount Warning) is the old central vent. Along the coast, lighthouses stand at Point Danger and Fingal Head, and the old railway line from Murwillumbah is now a 24 km rail trail. It makes a quieter alternative base to the Gold Coast, 34 km north.

variants: Wollumbin's summit track is closed, and NPWS will decide its future with Aboriginal custodians. The park stays open for the Lyrebird rainforest walk, picnic areas and camping at Breakfast Creek, so check park alerts before driving out.
Queensland does not observe daylight saving, so in summer the clocks change an hour across the border from Tweed Heads to Coolangatta. NSW venues such as the Tweed Regional Gallery run on NSW time.
The rail trail's open Tweed section is 24 km one way, from Murwillumbah Railway Station to Crabbes Creek, so plan a return shuttle or bike hire; the trail website lists both.
The Wollumbin summit track and Aboriginal Place are closed. Plan on the park's shorter rainforest walk instead, and check NPWS alerts for the current status.
Gold Coast Airport at Coolangatta is about 5 km from Tweed Heads, and Brisbane is about 65 minutes away by the Pacific Motorway. The airport does not run around the clock.
The Tweed Regional Gallery is open Wednesday to Sunday, 10 am to 4 pm, with a free guided tour at 11:30 am. It closes over Christmas week.
Check the NPWS alerts before heading to Wollumbin: the summit track is closed, though the Lyrebird track and picnic areas are open.
In daylight saving months New South Wales is an hour ahead of Queensland, so a meal in Coolangatta can be on a different clock from your hotel in Tweed Heads.
Murwillumbah is about 23 km inland by road along the Tweed Valley Way, the old Pacific Highway, and is the start of both the rail trail and the gallery visit.
